articleTitle: Analysis and Reflection on the Situation of Industrial Information Security Ransomware Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Ransomware has been rampant around the world recently, infecting tens of thousands of devices and systems and raising security alarms for the global industrial information industry. In this paper, we provide a thorough analysis of industrial ransomware attacks in four aspects: staged differences, attack characteristics, industrial patterns, and enterprise security protection, by studying the current industrial ransomware attack cases and risk status. Finally, to reduce the threat of ransomware in the industrial sector and enhance the capacity of industrial information security protection, this paper proposes countermeasures and recommendations in five areas: strengthening the construction of security protection systems, testing and evaluation, monitoring and emergency response, data protection, and legislative oversight.

articleTitle: Empirical Study of the IPv4 and IPv6 Networks at the Autonomous System Level
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In this paper, based on the recent data (up to July, 2022), we empirically investigate the evolution of the IPv4 and IPv6 Internet topologies at the autonomous system (AS) level. We find that both networks are growing with time, while the IPv4 network is much greater in scale (including the number of nodes and links), but smaller in link density (average degree). The cumulative degree distribution of each network exhibits a double power-law form, which is different from the early observations. Moreover, we show that the innermost cores (obtained by the k-core decomposition algorithm) in two networks are largely overlapped. Finally, by inspecting the clustering coefficient and the degree correlations, we demonstrate that the two networks are hierarchically organized. Another traditional indicator, i.e., the normalized rich-club coefficient proposed by Colizza et al., fails to capture the hierarchy property of the IPv4 and IPv6 networks. Nevertheless, if we generalize the concept of “rich club” by evaluating the richness of a node in terms of “coreness” (not in terms of “degree”), we still observe such phenomenon at some times.

articleTitle: The Report of Standardization for Blockchain-Based Digital Right Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Under the threat of digitalization of creations, the traditional digital right management method exposes several problems, including high entering&maintaining costs and low transaction efficiency. Meanwhile, the booming development of blockchain technology shows the potential to harness these issues. Thus, this paper aims to deliver an analysis report of the standardization situation for blockchain-based DRM systems In front, we analyze the current situation of copyright management in both relevant standards and applications. Meanwhile, two general DRM systems based on alliance blockchain and a DRM platform based on public blockchain are demonstrated respectively to satisfy the needs of copyright authentication, judicial safeguards, and digital assets or right transaction.

articleTitle: Service Resources Mining Based on Association Rules
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In recent years, the common service resources mining for cloud business operation under micro-service architecture has been a key problem in the intelligent operation and maintenance of cloud platforms. How to identify system resource anomaly to complete comprehensive monitoring and analysis of the system is an predominant challenge to most existing methods. In this paper, we propose an improved Apriori algorithm based on comparing transaction ID sets, which addresses the bottleneck problems of the classic Apriori algorithm requiring multiple scans of the transaction database and generating a large number of candidate sets during processing. The algorithm utilizes the minimum support threshold to remove non frequent items, thereby achieving the goal of reducing the generated candidate set. Based on the improved Apriori algorithm, analyze the correlation between various attributes, standardize the relevant attributes first, and then conduct discretization processing. The combination of discretization attributes forms the chromosome sequence under the normal operation of the business system, and then analyze whether the monitoring data is within the existing chromosome range through a fixed time window (such as 1 hour). If not, judge whether there is an exception.

articleTitle: Cross-System Data Integration Based on Rule-Based NLP and Node2Vec
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In the era of Big data, a growing number of enterprises are paying attention to data governance and data services. Large enterprises (e.g., state grid corporations), have numerous information systems, which have caused issues such as inconsistent data standards, and different data storage methods. This makes it very difficult to share data information among different enterprises and departments. In this situation, enterprises have begin to use various methods to integrate data across different systems. In this study, we select the power industry and design a cross-system data fusion framework. Specifically, there are many types of power grid equipment, and the topology data, equipment data, and operation data associated with them are stored in different ways. For cross-system data, we first use equipment name information and design a ruled-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) technique to match the same data between different systems. However, the equipment names in different systems do not follow a strict and unified naming standard, which leads to a set of equipment nodes that cannot be accurately matched. To solve this issue, we use network structure information about equipment and design a node representation technique based on Node2vec. Based on the node representation, we further optimize the results of equipment matching. For evaluation, we use a cross-system dataset from a state grid corporation in China. Through experiments, we show that the proposed framework performs very well in cross-system data integration.

articleTitle: Anti-Breast Cancer Active Compound Screening Method Based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm and BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common diseases, and it is essential to develop effective anti-breast cancer drugs. Drug optimization modeling can improve drug screening efficiency and predict the activity and side effects of drug molecules. Developing compound activity prediction models is an effective application of drug optimization modeling. Traditional machine learning-based compound activity prediction models, such as statistical-based and deep learning-based methods, have limitations in their use and methodological flaws, leading to problems such as low accuracy and efficiency in predicting compound activity. This paper proposes an anti-breast cancer active compound screening method based on simulated annealing algorithm and BP neural network to address these issues. Through experiments that compare this method to other methods, the effectiveness and superiority of this method have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Model of Shearer Cutting Motor Based on Fuzzy Neural Network and Expert System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Insufficient fault data or label data has always been one of the reasons for the low accuracy of fault diagnosis models. In this paper, we propose a novel fault diagnosis method named Fuzzy Neural Network with Expert System (ES-FNN), which combines fuzzy neural networks with expert systems to improve diagnosis accuracy. Specifically, ES-FNN introduces expert knowledge to participate in training set construction, thus avoids the impact of small data set on model training. Furthermore, the combination of fuzzy logic system and neural network can fuzzifies the input information and strengthen inference. Finally, we compared the performance of the proposed model with other three classical neural network algorithms: BP, GABP, RBF and ES-FNN. Results under the same settings demonstrate that the proposed model effectively learns fuzzy rules and achieves the highest diagnosis accuracy among the compared models.

articleTitle: Improved Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm Based on Arctangent Inertia Weight
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: An improved Grey Wolf Optimization (AGWO) algorithm based on arctangent inertia weight strategy is proposed to address the slow convergence speed and low optimization accuracy of the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm. The AGWO algorithm has non-linear characteristics and can better balance the global and local search capabilities of the algorithm. Under special situation, AGWO can degenerate into GWO, AGWO is an extent of GWO. The search performance of AGWO is tested on five classic test functions. The experimental results show that AGWO has higher optimization performance than four classical swarm intelligence algorithms.

articleTitle: Exploring the Factors and Influence Mechanisms of User Loyalty for Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: This article explores the antecedent variables and mechanisms of influence for user satisfaction with generative AI. The variables and models were extracted through a literature review, combining the technology acceptance model, self-determination theory, and anthropomorphism and perceptual intelligence as two domain-specific influences on generative AI. Data was collected by distributing a questionnaire to conduct an empirical study. The empirical results showed that perceived usefulness, perceived intelligence, and anthropomorphism have a significant positive impact on user satisfaction, while the mechanisms that influence loyalty are through the individual's internal perception rather than external pressure. The paper proposes a user loyalty model for generative AI that extends loyalty research to the emerging field of generative AI and provides guidance for the rapid iterative development of generative AI.

articleTitle: Threat-Aware Data Transmission in Software-Defined Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Characterized by flexible network management and control, Software-Defined Networks (SDN) has emerged as a promising networking paradigm in recent years. With data transmission paths centrally controlled in SDN, high efficiency and quality of data transmission can be reasonably expected. However, these benefits could easily be compromised, if cyber threats targeted the data transmission paths, particularly the transmitting nodes, cannot be well mitigated or tolerated. To address this challenging issue, we in this paper propose a Threat-aware Data Transmission (TDT) mechanism for SDN. Prior to this, first we establish a mathematical data transmission model for SDN, and then we design a threat intelligence based cyber threat evaluation approach for transmitting nodes. Numerical results demonstrate the outperformance of the proposed scheme over existing studies.

articleTitle: Application of Real-Time Big Data Technology in Complex Power Engineering Management
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: This paper introduces the complexity of power grid engineering management and the difficulty of the timeliness of power grid big data. At the same time, the construction of the existing platform is briefly described, and the architecture and contributions of this paper are introduced. In terms of related work, this paper presents the current state of application of the complex generic environment big data platform, power grid engineering management technology and power grid engineering management big data analysis technology. Regarding RTBDT technology, this paper describes the framework, data cleaning technology, data synchronization technology, multi-stream data alignment technology, and batch stream integration data analysis technology. Finally, the paper presents the functionality and results of the example platform and summarizes the research in this paper.

articleTitle: A Data Sharing and Access Control Model Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In the era of data-centric driving enterprise business, how to effectively control data access and securely share data between enterprises has become a common concern. While blockchain's distributed ledger solves this problem in some ways, blockchain's asymmetric encryption is only for one-to-one secure transmissions. Therefore, this paper uses attribute-based encryption to propose a data sharing and access control model for enterprise data. Designed to achieve more precise access control and secure sharing. After comparison, the model can better solve the problem of data access control within enterprises and data sharing between enterprises.

articleTitle: Towards Accurate and Efficient Super Spreader Detection with Sketching
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Super spreaders are the flow that have a large number of distinct connections (also called spread), which related with many threats to networks. Estimating flow spread is the crucial step in super spreader detection. However, existing methods cannot achieve flow spread estimation in terms of accurate, efficient, and reversible simultaneously. All these characteristics is highly required for high-speed network measurement. In this paper, we propose MorphSketch, a new data structure that estimates flow spread for super spreader detection with high accuracy, memory efficiency, high throughput and reversibility. MorphSketch combines hashing with sampling to process packets in order to improve throughput. It uses self-morph bitmap to record spread information, which can adaptively enlarge the upper bound of spread estimation under limited memory usage to ensure accuracy and memory efficiency. Moreover, MorphSketch can track candidate super spreader by comparing corresponding spread information, which realizes reversibility in super spreader detection. We perform a series of performance evaluations on real world traffic trace. Experiment results demonstrate that under same memory usage, the MorphSketch significantly outperforms existing work in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Assessing the Risk of Heavy Metal Mixture Exposure and its Association with Cancer Mortality
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: This study examined the combined effects of lead, cadmium, and mercury exposure on malignant neoplasms-related mortality among 6,014 adults who participated in NHANES between 2003 and 2014. Using unsupervised clustering, individuals were stratified into different co-exposure patterns, with the high co-exposure group having a significantly higher risk of malignant neoplasms-related deaths compared to the low co-exposure group. The impact of co-exposure varied in subpopulations with different social/economic statuses. Older participants, low-income, alcohol consumption, men, non-Hispanic Black, and obese participants seemed to be more vulnerable to high co-exposure to the metals. Therefore, comprehensive strategies to prevent deaths from cancer should include efforts to reduce exposure to these toxic metals, especially in vulnerable subpopulations.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Method of Vehicle-Road-Cloud Collaborative System Security Situation Based on (CD)2-A Elastic Computing Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the booming of intelligent connected vehicles (ICVs), cybersecurity of vehicle-road-cloud collaborative system has attracted great attention, correspondingly information security assessment on it. Existing research on information security assessment in the field mainly focuses on the internet of vehicles (10V) particularly on intelligent vehicle and specific vehicle components while the research on quantitative evaluation method developed for the security situation of vehicle-road-cloud collaborative system is a blank. At present, The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is a relatively approved approach for information security assessment, however it still challenges a lot due to subjective and arbitrary assert standards, even inefficiency operating in the presence of multiple evaluation objects. To handle the issues, the paper proposes an evaluation method of vehicle-road-cloud collaborative systems security situation based on the (CD)2-A elastic computing framework. In the method, the vehicle-road-cloud collaborative system is divided by a hierarchical model like sub-system level, component level, etc. Accordingly, the vulnerability of component level is evaluated from scores of CVSS and DREAD model elastically by the C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>R-DEA method and security situation of subsystem by AHP, eventually the security situation evaluation value of the whole system is settled. Given by calculation for practical ICVs attacked data from the industry reports, the method proposed in this paper is proved effective and more applicable in the security assessment of vehicle-road-cloud collaborative system.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Security Analysis Framework Based on Threat Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence technology accelerates technological progress and promotes social development, but also brings many security problems. Machine learning models may be affected, deceived, controlled or destroyed at different stages, e.g. training and inference, which may lead to serious consequences. In view of the main stages of the life cycle of machine learning, we summarizes the related attack and defense technologies based on threat matrix, makes a comprehensive and systematic analysis on the security issues of machine learning, and puts forward several security protection suggestions for intelligent information systems.

articleTitle: Bi-ETC: A Bidirectional Encrypted Traffic Classification Model Based on BERT and BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: While packet encryption technology provides user privacy protection, it also brings challenges to traffic classification. Traditional traffic classification technologies based on packet fields or payload data content are becoming powerless in the face of encrypted traffic. Although traffic encryption technology can hide data content, it cannot change the inherent characteristics of application traffic. Therefore, how to classify encrypted traffic by mining traffic features has become a topic of widespread concern. An enormous amount of research shows that machine learning algorithms achieve good results in encrypted traffic classification. However, there is still room for improvement. For example, deep learning methods require a large amount of labeled training data, and it is difficult for pre-trained models to capture the associated features of long sequences of packet. This paper propose a Bidirectional encrypted traffic classification model based on BERT and BiLSTM(Bi-ETC), by inserting [CLS]Token at the connection of Token sequence between BERT and BiLSTM, strengthens BiLSTM's focus on packet-level features while maintaining BilSTM's capture of Token sequence context. Experimental results show that the Bi-ETC model is superior to all proposed classification methods on the ISCX VPN dataset, reaching 99.43%in F1 score and 99.7%in accuracy.

articleTitle: Towards Scale-Aware Self-Supervised Multi-Frame Depth Estimation with IMU Motion Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In recent years, self-supervised depth and ego- motion estimation have attracted extensive research attention. Self-supervised monocular depth estimation can effectively learn information from texture-less and non-Lambertian surfaces. However, the monocular methods' accuracy is limited owing to the depth ambiguity in the imaging principles of monocular cameras. On the other hand, multi-frame methods usually have higher depth accuracy benefitting from the geometric constraints of Multi-View Stereo (MVS). However, MVS is sensitive to non- Lambertian surfaces, moving objects, and texture-less regions, which often leads to wrong estimation. In addition, both methods are difficult to obtain the absolute scale result owing to the essential scale ambiguity of monocular images. To resolve the above problems, we propose the FusionDepth, a scale-aware method that fuses the information from monocular depth estimation, multi-frame depth estimation, and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) in this paper. FusionDepth fuses multi-frame depth estimation and monocular depth estimation through an uncertainty mask to realize complementary advantages. It further fuses IMU information with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to learn an absolute scale metric. To run the model in real-time on resource-limited devices, we compact the framework by sharing the encoder and taking two lightweight decoders to lower the expense of pose prediction and the depth prediction of MVS. We verify FusionDepth's effectiveness on the KITTI benchmark and the comparison experiments indicate our method is efficient and accurate.

articleTitle: An Image Emotion Classification Method Based on Supervised Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: This article proposes an image emotion classification model based on supervised contrastive learning, which includes two modules of low-level feature extraction and deep emotion feature extraction, and feature fusion is used to enhance the overall perception of image emotion. In the low-level feature extraction module, the LBP (Local Binary Patterns) algorithm is used to extract texture features of images. In the deep emotion feature extraction module, supervised contrastive learning is introduced to narrow the intra-class distance between the same emotion images and expand the inter-class distance between different emotion images, so as to improve the classification performance of the overall model. Comprehensive experiments on the FI emotion dataset show that the proposed model has good performance for image emotion classification.

articleTitle: Syntactic Enhanced Euphemisms Identification Based on Graph Convolution Networks and Dependency Parsing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: To evade content moderation policies, social media users adopt euphemisms (also called algospeak, which refers to a benign-looking alternative to sensitive content) to obfuscate their true intentions. Euphemisms identification task aims at understanding the confusing expressions and interpreting the true meanings of euphemisms, which plays a key role in recent euphemisms analysis. The leading euphemisms identification method defines this problem as a text classification task, which establishes a mapping between euphemisms and corresponding real-meaning words in a specific area through fine-grained classification. However, the traditional classification methods leverage explicit textual semantic features, where specific terms and oral swearing in user speech from forums may introduce bias to the classification results on specific areas and limit the performance of euphemisms identification. In this work, we propose SyGCN for euphemisms identification task. Specifically, SyGCN captures the explicit syntactic features by using dependency parsing tree as extended features and integrates syntactic features and semantic features into the Graph Convolution Network to enhance the identification performance. We conduct experiments on three sensitive categories and demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. The experimental results show that our model can effectively utilize the syntactic structure information of dependency parsing to improve the performance of euphemisms identification.

articleTitle: A Review of User Identity Linkage Across Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the rapid development of social networks, the services provided by social platforms are becoming more and more diversified, which attracts many people to participate in different social network. If the accounts of the same user in different social networks can be identified, a more comprehensive information about the user can be integrated. Therefore, some hidden information can be unearthed and a complete user profile can be formed, making it better applied to recommendation systems and network security. User identity linkage aims to identify accounts belonging to the same natural person across social networks, which has attracted a lot of attention in recent years. In this paper, we discuss the current research and development trend of user identity linkage. First, we introduce the basic concepts and the user information used in this technology. Then we summarize the existing techniques based on attributes, generated content, and social relationships. Further we list several common evaluation metrics. Finally, we provide several promising research directions for the future.

articleTitle: Blockchain Storage Method Based on Erasure Code
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Blockchain, as an emerging distributed database, effectively addresses the issue of centralized storage in IoT data, where storage capacity cannot match the explosive growth in devices and data scale, as well as the contradictions arising from centralized data management concerning data privacy and security concerns. To alleviate the problem of excessive pressure on single-point storage and ensure data security, a blockchain data storage method based on erasure codes is proposed. This method involves constructing mathematical functions that describe the data to split the original block data into multiple fragments and add redundant slices. These fragments are then encoded and stored in different locations using a circular hash space with the addition of virtual nodes to ensure load balancing among nodes and reduce situations where a single node stores too many encoded data blocks, effectively enhancing the storage space utilization efficiency of the distributed storage database. The blockchain storage method stores encoded data digest information such as storage location, creation time, and hashes, allowing for the tracing of the origin of encoded data blocks. In case of accidental loss or malicious tampering, this enables effective recovery and ensures the integrity and availability of data in the network. Experimental results indicate that compared to traditional blockchain approaches, this method effectively reduces the storage pressure on nodes and exhibits a certain degree of disaster recovery capability.

articleTitle: CoReg: Membership Privacy Protection via Collaborative Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Machine learning is widely used in many areas, however, it has been proved that machine learning models are prone to leak sensitive information of the training data. For instance, the adversary could precisely infer whether a sample belongs to the target model's training set with membership inference attacks (MIAs). To mitigate the membership inference risks, we propose a novel defense framework, named CoReg. It trains multiple sub-models and they regularize each other with a novel collaborative regularization. With this method, we could reduce the membership leakage risks by enforcing the model to have similar behavior on members and non-members, while maintaining high classification performances. Furthermore, we propose an adversarial output control module to select the output of the least risky sub-model as the final output. We carry out extensive experiments on three datasets and verify that CoReg could achieve better protection effects against MIAs than baselines while maintaining high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Building a High-Performance Data Channel for the Federal Cyber Range
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: To efficiently support large-scale simulation traffic in the Federal Cyber Range, it is necessary to establish a high-performance data channel between cyber ranges. This channel utilizes the VPN protocol for secure encryption, ensuring the secure transmission of user data. WireGuard has the characteristics of being faster and more streamlined than traditional VPN technology. To address the issue that the Network Interface Card does not support the distribution of encrypted VPN traffic, a traffic-splitting mechanism has been proposed for WireGuard VPN. This method is based on XDP technology and bypasses the kernel network protocol stack, which can reduce the processing delay of packets and distribute encrypted traffic evenly to different CPU cores. A scheduling algorithm based on the earliest departure time is used when sending packets. By combining the retransmission packet detection algorithm proposed in this paper, the priority of retransmission packets and other interested flows can be flexibly controlled. The system's test results from multiple perspectives such as bandwidth and delay show that compared with the Linux kernel module WireGuard solution, the bandwidth utilization rate of the link network is increased by more than 2.5 times, and the transmission delay is effectively reduced by more than 80%.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Learning for Game Review Classification with Emotion and Sarcasm Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a widely used technique to identify the emotion tendency of a piece of text. As the number of video games and players continues to increase, the task of automating emotion computing for game reviews is essential for both game platforms and developers. The former can recommend good and suitable games to users, while the latter can provide game developers with suggestions for improvement. However, there are few affective computing studies and models in the field of game reviews. Therefore, this paper investigates the performance of several traditional sentiment classification models on game review datasets and deduces several possible reasons for model performance degradation based on misclassified samples. Based on these preliminary studies, we believe that sarcasm, game context, and comparison are the three main reasons leading to the decline in classifier performance. We conclude that a satisfactory model requires the following characteristics: sarcasm detection, game contextualization, and key emotion capture. Based on this, we design a multi-tasking game review classification model integrating sarcasm detection and emotion analysis modules. Experiments on two real datasets from the Steam platform demonstrate that our approach has superior performance compared to mainstream sentiment classification models.

articleTitle: Research Ideas on Network Security Experiment and Appraisal of Avionics System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Avionic systems constitute a significant component of modern military and civilian aircraft, serving as a crucial technological means to ensure the accomplishment of designated missions and safe flight operations. They also play a pivotal role in determining the overall performance of contemporary military and civilian aviation equipment. However, with the rapid development of aviation technology and the high degree of interconnectivity in avionic systems, an increasing number of network security threats have emerged. While numerous approaches have been proposed to address the network threats encountered in avionic systems, none have comprehensively covered all network threats pertaining to avionic systems. Furthermore, there is a lack of a unified standard for assessing network security issues specific to avionic systems. Therefore, this paper presents a comprehensive approach to constructing an aviation electronic system network security experimental system. This approach also provides a reference standard that can serve as a theoretical foundation for subsequent research projects and scientific studies on security issues in avionic systems. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed comprehensive approach in mitigating various network security threats, while also establishing a standard for designing aviation electronic system network security solutions.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Knowledge Representation: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: A modality refers to the way people receive information, such as vision, hearing, tactile sense, etc. If a task or data set involves multiple modalities, it is called multi-modal. In recent years, there has been more and more research in the field of multi-modal. Especially in the area of vision and language, many studies combine the excellent work of CV and NLP. With the development of knowledge graphs and representation, many works have also begun utilizing external knowledge to improve performance. To explore how multi-modal information and knowledge are utilized, this paper provides a comprehensive survey on multi-modal knowledge representation, which has never been systematically discussed. To facilitate the discussion of how the models combine and utilize multi-modal information and knowledge, we categorize multi-modal knowledge representation methods into two frameworks: explicit multi-modal knowledge representation and implicit multi-modal knowledge representation. For each framework, we introduce some typical models in vision-and-Ianguage, to help new researchers in this field understand the multi-modal knowledge representation model better. In addition, we introduce some downstream tasks and propose some important directions for future work.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Bluetooth AOA Indoor Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the continuous updates, iterations, and promotion of Bluetooth standard specifications, Bluetooth has filled many gaps in existing indoor positioning technologies with its comprehensive technical specifications, rich application ecosystem, and a series of advantages such as low power consumption and low cost in hardware. Especially after the introduction of ADA/AOD direction finding technology in the Bluetooth 5.1 protocol specification, Bluetooth positioning can achieve high accuracy at the sub-meter level. Therefore, Bluetooth-based indoor positioning has become a current research hotspot and an important future development trend. However, there is currently relatively limited research and application of positioning algorithms and positioning systems based on Bluetooth, and there is no standardized set of positioning algorithms and positioning systems. Therefore, this paper proposes research and design on Bluetooth AOA positioning algorithm and Bluetooth AOA indoor positioning system. Through testing in actual indoor scenarios, the algorithm has been validated to achieve sub-meter positioning accuracy, and the entire positioning system has successfully completed the entire process from deployment to application demonstration.

articleTitle: Identifying Mobile Application Over Shadowsocks with Single-Direction Traffic
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: An anonymous proxy system, such as Shadowsocks, creates a secure tunnel between the user and the proxy server, effectively concealing the raw traffic from any network elements along the transmission path. While this enhances user privacy, it also presents a challenge for traffic inspection. Identifying the application associated with the traffic is crucial, but it can be a challenging task when dealing with encrypted traffic over Shadowsocks. Current research on encrypted traffic analysis assumes that bi-directional traffic can be used for testing. However, in reality, traffic inspection is typically performed on gateways, and in a large cross-regional network environment there are often multiple ingress and egress gateways. This means that inbound and outbound traffic usually travel through different gateways, making it essential to be able to identify the application with single-direction Shadowsocks encrypted traffic. This paper presents a novel method for identifying mobile applications through Shadowsocks encrypted single-direction traffic. To achieve this, we have designed a sliding-window based feature extraction mechanism that can effectively extract features from single-direction traffic. Additionally, we have constructed three machine learning models, including random forest, XGBoost, and lightGBM, to classify the application type. To handle high data dimension and feature redundancy, we have also employed a feature selection scheme that keeps prediction accuracy while reducing the computational cost. We have conducted experiments using popular social network mobile applications, and our results demonstrate that our method achieves promising classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Quantitative Dynamic Scalability Model and Analysis of Blockchain Database System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: The scalability of blockchain database systems has garnered considerable attention. This paper introduces a quantitative dynamic scalability (QDS) model and presents two metrics: throughput growth (TG) following an increase in available resources, and the number of resources that users find acceptable under the maximum latency (UL) level. The TG model's calculation necessitates the slope of throughput growth versus available resources, which can be determined using the universal scalability law (USL) model. We found that the non-sharded blockchain database cannot be entirely fitted and that the USL model cannot provide accurate slope values. Therefore, we developed a novel universal scalability law plus (USL+) model based on the classic USL model. Regarding the experimental evaluation, we verified the USL+'s less accuracy, particularly with a roughly 52% relative error (USL) and a 15% relative error (USL+) for larger node numbers. We then numerically simulated the QDS model and examined the impact of different data sets, finding that the error was smaller with more similar configurations. Finally, we investigated different protocols using the QDS algorithm and found that RingBFT's scalability was better with only two shards, while SharPer was better with 50 shards.

articleTitle: A Blackbox Fuzzing Based on Automated State Machine Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Currently, protocol fuzzing techniques mainly employ two approaches: greybox fuzzing based on mutation and blackbox fuzzing based on generation. Greybox fuzzing techniques use message exchanges between the protocol server and actual clients as seeds, and generate test cases through mutation. Although this approach can provide coverage information of the SUT's code and state space through instrumentation and feedback, its drawback lies in the relatively random mutation strategy, which makes it challenging to validate the SUT's message verification process. This paper addresses this limitation by utilizing artificial intelligence techniques to extract protocol state machines. It aims to overcome the reliance on manual work in blackbox fuzzing based on generation and leverage its advantages to generate more effective fuzzing test cases. The study utilizes Prompt-Learning technology to analyze the semantic information in protocol RFC documents, obtain corresponding intermediate representations, and extract protocol state machines from these representations. Taking the BGP protocol as an experimental subject, the experimental results demonstrate a certain level of accuracy in the obtained protocol state machines and the ability to generate test cases from these state machines, thereby enhancing the automation level of protocol fuzzing.

articleTitle: Cluster Analysis of Target Events Based on Multidimensional Network Traffic Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: The clustering algorithm is widely used in the analysis of target events of network traffic data due to the characteristics of no pre-labeled data and interpretability, which can analyze and mine the similar or identical feature patterns that the target exhibits in specific events. Aiming at the problem that the traditional DBSCAN algorithm cannot effectively identify and divide fine-grained clusters when facing local areas with different densities, an improved DBSCAN method based on multi-dimensional network traffic characteristics is proposed. Firstly, multi-dimensional network traffic characteristics are extracted based on time series network traffic data, and then from the perspective of clustering, Pearson correlation coefficient is introduced based on the traditional DBSCAN algorithm to further refine the division of cluster sets. By comparing the traditional DBSCAN algorithm with the improved algorithm on the network traffic data set obtained in the real network environment, the experimental results show that the improved algorithm is better than the traditional DBSCAN algorithm in comprehensive performance, and the accuracy rate is increased by up to 8%.

articleTitle: SSDAEE: Semi-Supervised Data-Augmented Event Extraction for Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Although the general event extraction model has achieved good results in the standard data sets, there is a gap in the extraction results in low-resource environments. The general event extraction model still has room for improvement in the performance of special fields. Therefore, this paper proposes a semi-supervised reading comprehension event extraction model adapted to transfer learning, based on improved UDA for data enhancement, called SSDAEE, which can increase the accuracy of reading comprehension event type recognition. SSDAEE has a good performance on the public opinion data set. It can not only enhance a small number of supervised data in low-resource fields with unsupervised data but also improve the generalization ability of the model. Experiments show that when only 5% unsupervised data is used, the F1 score of SSDAEE on the public opinion data set is increased by 9% compared with the fully supervised model, and by 2% compared with other semi-supervised models.

articleTitle: Efficient Lightweight Intrusion Detection Method for IoT OS: A Study on the Application of Multi-Teacher Distillation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: As the second important security measure behind the firewall, network intrusion detection provides effective assurance for computer network security. In recent years, deep learning (DL) has emerged as a promising approach for enhancing intrusion detection and achieving high experimental accuracy. However, due to performance limitations caused by resource consumption, deep neural network models with high requirements for floating-point calculations cannot be directly applied to Internet of Things devices. In our study, the decision tree is initially employed to reduce the feature dimension and extract spatial features. We then combine the teacher network based on the Bi-GRU algorithm to capture the temporal traffic features, achieving an accuracy rate of 99.41% on the CICIDS2017 dataset. We use these two high-accuracy models as teachers for multi-teacher knowledge distillation. The student model adopts a lightweight network architecture, with a scale only 2.5% of that of the teacher model. Finally, we compare the performance of the teacher network and the student network on Internet of Things devices. We find that the accuracy loss is only 0.09% compared to the teacher network. Moreover, the accuracy for DDoS attacks has been improved by 30.1% compared to the non-distilled model. The IDS framework we designed is well-suited for scenarios such as the Internet of Vehicles and can be integrated with the cloud to update the device-side model and enhance system security.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Secure Data Sharing Approach with Proxy Re-Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In today's digital economy, data sharing has become imperative for advancing economic growth and technology development, as multi-party collaboration requires secure data exchange. During data sharing, upholding data security and privacy is paramount. However, existing data sharing solutions mostly rely on cloud storage and transfer, which have risks of single-point failure and compromise privacy and security. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel solution that leverages proxy re-encryption and digital watermarking technologies, and employs blockchain to achieve equivalent access control functions based on the cloud environment, thereby mitigating the single point of failure issue. Moreover, our solution can effectively prevent data requesters from illegally sharing data with others. If any requester leaks data without authorization, we can trace the source based on the watermark embedded in the leaked data. In summary, our proposed solution enables more secure and privacy-preserving data sharing, which can potentially benefit a wide range of data sharing applications.

articleTitle: Analysis and Research of Neural Network Adversarial Samples for Power Grid Security
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In the electric power information system security attack and defense in the industry, the use of big data adversarial samples to attack the neural network model can enhance the authenticity of the adversarial samples. This paper strengthens the research on the authenticity of the samples by analyzing and studying the generation of neural network adversarial samples and simulated at-tack tests. Through a variety of experimental methods, for the improvement of complex neural network adversarial samples, the generation method of semantic adversarial samples is improved and perfected, and adversarial disturbances are added. The experimental results show that after ComDefend and feature compression defense processing, the authenticity is improved by at least 30% compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Flow Anomaly Detection with Differential Optimal Feature Subspace
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of network scale and increasing complexity, the application of the Internet of Things (IoT) is becoming more extensive. However, it is also vulnerable to various abnormal attacks, making security problems increasingly significant. Typically, traffic data dimensions are relatively large, and selecting features effectively is a key research issue. Addressing the aforementioned problems, this paper analyzes network traffic data and proposes a method(DOFS) to select the optimal feature subspace for different types of attacks, and verifies its effectiveness by comparative experiments. Then the T-S feature selection algorithm is improved, and DOFS is applied to the improved T-S feature selection algorithm, and the usability of the method is verified by experiments. By obtaining feature importance scores, the best feature subspace is selected for each type of traffic category. The method is verified using the network flow dataset CIC2018 and a real-world flow dataset. Experimental evaluations on diverse datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing feature selection algorithms under different evaluation metrics, while exhibiting efficient time over-head and strong generalization ability. The results highlight the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed approach in IoT flow anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Universal Adversarial Perturbation From Dominant Feature For Speaker Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have greatly improved speaker recognition performance. However, DNNs are vulnerable to imperceptible adversarial example, which has attracted the attention in both academic and industrial areas in recent years. Although many elegant adversarial attack methods have been proposed, few of them studied Universal Adversarial Perturbation (UAP) against speaker recognition. In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm from the perspective of dominant features to generate UAP to mislead speaker recognition DNNs. Our method uses dominance as an optimization objective, and designs a tiny neural network to improve the efficiency. We conduct experiments on the TIMIT dataset and our method has achieved state-of-the-art results regarding attack success rate and imperceptibility. Moreover, leveraging the concept of dominant feature, our method significantly improves the training speed and can generate UAP more efficiently.

articleTitle: Graph Pattern Matching Based Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Method for Cloud Resource Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In recent years, cloud computing technology has been widely used in various industries. The cloud platform architecture has thoroughly realized high scalability, high stability and low maintenance cost. However, along with the development of geometric growth in the number of micro-applications, cloud platform O&M such as abnormal monitoring and fault location of large-scale micro-services is facing new difficulties and challenges. Traditional cloud platform operation and maintenance work mainly relies on human experience to analyze a large number of indicators to determine whether there is a failure, which is very inefficient and relies heavily on expert opinions. To address the above issues, this paper applies graph pattern matching technology to the cloud platform. In the face of metrics monitoring data, link topology data, log data, and cloud resource data of the whole life cycle of micro-services, we design graph patterns based on existing cloud resource data, and then look for them in the existing fault graph to determine whether faults occur and achieve intelligent operation and maintenance of cloud resource operation. Experimental results on four datasets show that our approach is more effective than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Network Security Evaluation for Space-Ground Integrated Networks Based on Network Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) have become an important direction of future network development. However, SGINs face many security threats because of the multidimensional heterogeneity of their structure. Therefore, effective network security evaluation is an indispensable part of SGIN security research. Most existing network security evaluations are oriented toward network environments with simple structures and small scales and cannot be applied to SGINs. This paper reports the simulation of realistic SGIN scenarios through network simulation. Based on such network simulation, this paper proposes a network security evaluation suitable for SGINs that realizes the evaluation of the security risks and threats to SGINs in order to further improve their security. First, a SGIN security evaluation architecture is constructed to hierarchically describe the SGIN security evaluation process. Then, considering the characteristics of SGINs and abnormal network behavior characteristics, a SGIN security evaluation index system is designed, laying a foundation for the security evaluation of SGINs. Second, in view of the requirements of security evaluation data collection, a data collection method with multiple categories of indices is proposed, which not only guarantees the effectiveness of data collection but also improves the collection efficiency. Finally, based on game theory, a network security evaluation model is designed for the systematic security evaluation requirements of SGINs. This model realizes the effective evaluation of the effects of abnormal network behavior while accounting for subjective intentions and objective patterns. Experimental results show that the proposed technique can effectively gather information about system data resources through data collection. At the same time, the proposed network security evaluation model conforms to the patterns of abnormal network behavior and effectively meets the needs of security evaluation for SGINs.

articleTitle: Self-Disclosure Causality Detection: Discover What Cause the Self-Disclosure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Self-disclosure is defined as personal information a person discloses to other individuals or organizations. As social media grows, the seriousness of self-disclosure comes to the fore. Most research work on self-disclosure has been limited to self-disclosure detection, with little relevant research on the causes that lead to self-disclosure. However, plenty of self-disclosures are triggered during interactions, so it is more important to find the corresponding reasons for these self-disclosures during interactions to better detect self-disclosures. In this paper, we explore a novel task, namely Self-disclosure Causality Detection(SCD), aiming to detect the causality between interactive behaviors. The SCD task is more challenging because it requires capturing the causality between interactions and samples of SCD are unevenly distributed across different types of information leakage. Therefore, we propose a method with prompt learning called the Self-disclosure Causality Detection Model Between Interaction(SCDMBI) to capture the causality between the interaction behaviors of SCD. We build a dataset for the analysis of causes of self-information leakage called Cl-Aff Causality(CC) dataset which is divided into four categories according to the type of information leaked: family relationship, occupation, geographic location, and entity. We evaluate our method on the dataset CC. Experimental results show that our method can effectively detect sentences that lead to self-disclosure.

articleTitle: Analyzing Security Attacks Against Platoon of Intelligent and Connected Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the development of communications-related intelligent transport applications, intelligent and connected vehicles (ICVs) can more efficiently solve the problems brought by the rapid growth of road traffic, but it also introduces severe cyber security problems. In this paper, we take platoon, an intelligent transport application of ICVs, to analyze the impact of cyber attacks. Firstly we proposed an attack simulation and analysis framework, then many rigorous tests on a simulated platoon were executed, which using four types of attack model, finally the analysis results was shown. Analysis results show that security attacks can cause serious impact on platoon, and different type of attacks can disturb platoon randomly or regularly, but after the attack platoon can restore to normal which shows the system resilience.

articleTitle: Collaborative Learning for Cross-Organizational Data Sharing Using Hyperledger Fabric
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: The rise of edge networking presents both opportunities and challenges. The ever-expanding array of IoT devices generates vast amounts of data, enabling collaboration and smart applications. However, managing decentralized data, resolving heterogeneity, and ensuring privacy poses challenges. The combination of blockchain and federated learning offers a solution. But trust management, inefficiencies, and ambiguous assessment of data contribution have become new obstacles. In this paper, we propose a data sharing model that supports cross-organizational collaborative learning based on Hyperledger Fabric, in order to enhance the high-quality data sharing of collaborative learning and improve the effect of learning. The experimental results show that the proposed model can realize decentralized and efficient data sharing and improve the accuracy and stability of collaborative learning under acceptable communication load.

articleTitle: Based on Linkable Ring Signature Map Review Scheme for Zero-Trust Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: The real-time map plays a vital role in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) navigation. Compared with the existing map review, the real-time map review method is based on crowdsensing enabling faster data updates and shortening the map period from map collection to service. However, the crowdsensing method requires frequent interaction between the vehicle and nearby devices or servers, increasing the risk of user privacy leakage. How to ensure the privacy of users is a challenge in the real-time map review. Starting from the typical architecture of IoV and combining the core idea of zero-trust “never trust, continuous verification”, IoV-ZT conceptual model architecture is designed. This paper proposes a based on linkable ring signature map review scheme for zero-trust autonomous vehicles (LRSMR). In the LRSMR, a linkable ring signature based on the SM2 digital signature algorithm is used to protect user identity privacy and ensures while ensuring signature linkability by hiding the identity of the actual signer in the ring. Through the requirement for user credit, the reliability of the review data is improved. At the same time, the distribution of rewards increases users' motivation. At last, the security analysis indicates that the LRSMR satisfies correctness, unforgeability, unconditional anonymity, linkability and nonslanderability. The simulation results illustrate that the LRSMR is efficient in terms of communication overhead and computation cost.

articleTitle: Adversarial Example Detection for Deep Neural Networks: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have been widely applied in various critical domains. However, they are vulnerable to the threat of adversarial examples. It is challenging to make deep neural networks inherently robust to adversarial examples, while adversarial example detection offers advantages such as not affecting model classification accuracy. This paper introduces common adversarial attack methods and provides an explanation of adversarial example detection. Recent advances in adversarial example detection methods are categorized into two major classes: statistical methods and adversarial detection networks. The evolutionary relationship among different detection methods is discussed. Finally, the current research status in this field is summarized, and potential future directions are highlighted.

articleTitle: OIDMD: A Novel Open-Set Intrusion Detection Method Based on Mahalanobis Distance
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Intrusion detection has been a classic and challenging problem since new attacks emerge rapidly. Traditional methods are normally divided into two categories, anomaly detection and close-set detection. Anomaly detection methods cannot provide detailed diagnostic information about attacks, while close-set detection methods cannot cope with the constantly appearing unknown attacks. However, in real-world scenarios, intrusion detection methods have to detect known attacks while also identifying unknown ones. This is called open-set recognition which means that the detection model encounters unknown attacks that do not appear in the train phase. Some researchers have proposed open-set recognition methods to address the problem, but these methods are mainly based on Euclidean distance, which has two problems: (1) not taking into account the different scales of different feature (dimension) changes; (2) not considering the correlation between features. In this paper, we propose OIDMD that solves the open-set intrusion recognition based on the Mahalanobis distance. We conduct fine-grained attack classification of known attacks. Also, we conduct extensive experiments on the CICIDS2017 dataset and the results show that OIDMD outperforms existing methods for identifying unknown attacks, which confirms the effectiveness of open-set intrusion detection based on the Mahalanobis distance.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Knowledge Graph Enables Targeted Data Collection for Cybersecurity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Effective data collecting is crucial for comprehensively understanding and analyzing cyberspace security. As the data related cybersecurity is highly complicated which involves network traffic, system log, security alerts, etc. Traditional methods of data collection, such as total data collection and partial collection, are susceptible to data overload, resulting in a decrease in data analysis efficiency. Furthermore, these methods fail to emphasize the correlation among the collected data. To address these issues, we propose a targeted data collection framework based on cybersecurity knowledge graph in this paper. This framework aims to tailor the collection targets and establish specific collection rules based on different tasks and assets, thereby enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of cybersecurity data analysis. By examining data sources that may be impacted by cybersecurity vulnerabilities, the framework designs specific correlated collection rules for these sources. Comparative experiments with other data collection methods show that the proposed framework can reduce time consumption by 43% and storage space by 54% for the attack detection tasks.

articleTitle: An Interpretable Data-Driven Approach for Employee Ability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Employee ability assessment is significant to both individual employee development and organizational human resource management. However, the existing employee ability assessment in enterprises is mostly based on subjective judgment and still lacks an effective data-driven employee ability assessment model. Therefore, this paper proposes an interpretable Employee Ability Assessment Model (EAM) based on cognitive diagnosis. Experimental results on real datasets show that our model can not only accurately predict employee promotions, but also automatically perform employee ability assessment, which supports the accuracy and interpretability of our model. Our paper not only fills the gap in the field of ability diagnosis research, but also has important application value for corporate human resource management practice.

articleTitle: A Novel Concept-Driven Negative Sampling Mechanism for Enhancing Semanticity and Interpretability of Knowledge Graph Completion Task
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In recent years, it has witnessed the revival of knowledge engineering, which is characterized by the rapid growth of Knowledge Graph (KGs). Currently, Knowledge Graph Representation (KGR) and Completion (KGC) methods all use the methodology of scoring triple (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e_{h},r, e_{t}$</tex>) to judge its correctness. Wherein, in the procedure of conventional Negative Sampling (NS) and reasoning, it is easy to be affected by the low-quality and uncertainty of negative triples related to the given KG, resulting in some unpredictable and inexplicable wrong results that do not conform to commonsense. On the contrary, human beings with commonsense could easily solve this problem. For this reason, this paper proposes a novel mechanism to automatically capture commonsense (concept emphasized here) associated with current KG to provide more deterministic and interpretable semantic information from the fact triple, and further designs a concept-driven negative sampling strategy for commonsense understanding. Overall, a hybrid reasoning approach jointly driven by concept constraints (inter with KG) and fact triple guides (intra with KG), is presented to promote more effective learning and training procedure of KG's representation and completion. Experiments on real-world datasets, show that the proposed work could be used as a flexible plug-in unit to enhance the previous KG representation and completion models.

articleTitle: Multimodal Features Enhanced Named Entity Recognition Based on Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Chinese Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a very important subtask in the information extraction domain. Its purpose is to locate named entities in the text and classify them into predetermined categories. The key point of NER is to learn a high-quality representation of tokens. Recently, representation learning techniques have been introduced into NER due to their excellent performance in mining the semantics of texts and mastering their organization. In the field of Chinese, many studies introduce multimodal feature extraction schemes to enrich token representations, such as radical and word. However, the learning scheme of these auxiliary features is relatively complex and has difficulty learning the interactive relationship between features with a concatenation or MLP fusion method. To address these challenges, a Multimodal Chinese NER Model based on Self-attention Mechanism named MNER is proposed, which consists of a multimodal feature fusion module and an entity classification module. To study the informative characterization of tokens, a multimodal feature fusion module is proposed to exploit radical, character, and word information. In the multimodal feature fusion module, a self-attention mechanism is designed to integrate multimodal features based on the correlation between the features, which addresses the problem that existing methods have difficulty exploiting interaction information between features. A semantic-aware category modifier is proposed to enhance the CRF classification layer's performance. It increases entity discrimination by adjusting the embeddings of features according to the similarity between the token embeddings and embedding of each entity category, which widens the encoding gap between different entities and narrows the search scope for entity classification. Finally, the proposed MNER is compared with ten state-of-the-art methods on Weibo and Resume datasets, and the results show the superiority of our model on three metrics.

articleTitle: A Trust Usage Control Approach for Media Player Based on Intel SGX
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the rise of music streaming, users can easily access paid audio content on their devices. At the same time, music publishers require audio platforms to implement digital rights management (DRM) on devices to prevent illegal distribution of copyrighted audio. However, existing DRM schemes rely mainly on obscurity, which experienced reverse engineers can defeat. We propose a usage control scheme using trusted computing to address this problem. As an extension of DRM, usage control provides more data-related protection. By leveraging SGX to protect keys, we ensure encrypted audio files stored locally are not vulnerable to reverse decryption, effectively preventing pirated software from supplying pirated audio to users via APIs.

articleTitle: A Simplified Variant for Graph Convolutional Network Based Knowledge Graph Completion Model
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) serve as useful resources for various applications including machine learning, data mining, and artificial intelligence. Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims at reasoning over known (observed) facts and infer the missing (unobserved) relationships, to improve KG's coverage. Many recent works have laid stress on leveraging Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for KGC task, which obtain good representation learning ability for graph-structured data, and have achieved satisfactory results. However, GCN-based researches continue to improve these lines of models by introducing an increasingly complex feature space. Especially, the hyper-parameter space of conventional GCN-based KGC model is too huge, resulting in low computational efficiency and excessive storage pressure. To overcome this problem, this paper investigates a simplified and generic variant for GCN-based KGC model, and shows that simple changes in the architecture of the underlying architecture (with a Subtraction Operator and an Addition Operator), can compte with state-of-the-art GCN-based models. Therefore, this paper proposes a easy-to-accomplish plug-in unit, which could be loaded into any current GCN-based KGC architectures, and help them maximize the maintenance of native model's original performance while significantly reducing parameter scale.

articleTitle: A1BERT: A Language-Agnostic Graph Neural Network Model for Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In today's IT landscape, software systems are indispensable, yet vulnerable to cyberattacks. Traditional manual vulnerability detection methods are inadequate due to resource limitations. Consequently, making automating vulnerability detection in source code to be a crucial task. This paper introduces AlBERT, a practical, language-agnostic Graph Neural Network(GNN) model. AlBERT transforms source code into a graph-based format, enabling analysis of code structure and semantics. Residual connections effectively propagate information and condense it into a fixed-size vector for vulnerability prediction. AlBERT achieves promising results: 64% accuracy on the benchmark dataset, 79% on ReVeal, and 94% on MSR datasets. This paper also compares AlBERT to contemporary baseline models. AlBERT serves as a foundation for automated vulnerability detection.

articleTitle: Automatically Identifying Sentences with Attack Behavior from Cyber Threat Intelligence Reports
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: In recent years, the automated extraction of attack behaviors from Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) reports has proven to be effective in rapidly responding to cyber threats. When extracting attack behaviors from CTI, it is crucial to identify the sentences that describe these behaviors. Identifying attack sentences from reports can be challenging due to semantic overlap between attack and non-attack sentences. To address this problem, We propose a sentence-level attack behavior identification method that integrates the semantics of sentences and labels, called BCC. It effectively identifies sentences in reports that describe attack behavior. Specifically, the BCC model uses the BERT layer to model sentences and labels by learning their similarity. The BCC employs a sliding window in the CNN layer to capture the interaction of IOC-level attack behaviors. During the model training process, we discovered that using one-hot labels leads to overconfidence. To address this issue, we introduced the LCM layer to learn the similarity between sentences and labels, capturing semantic overlap among labels. For experimental evaluation, we collected CTI reports from MANDIANT and UNIT 42 to construct a sentence-level attack behavior dataset. The dataset consists of 8,000 samples from CTI reports as the baseline corpus, and an additional 3,000 positive examples of IOC-level attack behavior sentences were generated using a customized template to prompt ChatGPT, ensuring a balanced distribution of positive and negative samples. On this dataset, the BCC model achieved significant results in identifying attack behavior sentences, with an F1 score of 94.70%. This outperformed baseline models such as EXTRACTOR (94.18%) and TTPDrill (90.98%). To validate the effectiveness of BCC in extracting subsequent attack behaviors, we conducted an experiment using five manually annotated CTIs. The results show that the BCC model significantly improves the accuracy of attack behavior extraction.

articleTitle: FixGPT: A Novel Three-Tier Deep Learning Model for Automated Program Repair
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: Automatic program repair plays a crucial role in the software development and implementation. While deep learning-based approaches have made significant progress, one inherent challenge is the inefficiency in code representation, which hampers accurate patch generation. Furthermore, the training data used by these data-driven approaches may be limited, and they may not be able to capture the subtle differences between vulnerabilities and patches. To address these issues, FixGPT, we propose a three-tier deep learning model in the study. Specifically, a generative pre-trained transformer model is designed in the first tier to capture code characteristics and programming patterns. The second tier integrates a generation model based on the structure of neural machine translation, for the purpose of generating potential patches. Finally, a contrast model is introduced in the last tier to differentiate between the vulnerability and the patch. We also incorporate the Byte Pair Encoding approach to reduce the search space by converting identifiers into subwords. Detailed experimental studies have been carried out to evaluate the performance of FixGPT on two well-known benchmarking datasets: QuixBugs and Defects4J. The results demonstrated significant improvements in the effectiveness and accuracy in comparison with existing solutions. We complement these findings through the analysis of two case studies.

articleTitle: The Intelligent Information Search System IISI and Its Key Technologies for Internet Big Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: With the development of cyberspace and applications, Internet big data has become ubiquitous, which contains important information and knowledge. Correspondingly, the demand for intelligent search of Internet big data has also arisen. IISI, an intelligent information search system, can automatically collect Internet big data and use big data analysis, natural language processing and artificial intelligence technologies to intelligently analyze and process Internet big data, obtain valuable information and knowledge contained within and construct knowledge graphs. By accurately understanding the user's search intention, the system offers intelligent search of Internet big data. This research focuses on the key technologies of IISI system, which provides an intelligent search framework for Internet big data, based on which intelligent search engines in different application fields can be constructed. Function and performance tests show that the IISI system has high real-time performance and precision in the intelligent search for Internet big data, which meets the needs of intelligent search for Internet big data. IISI provides important reference for the implementation of the intelligent information search system for Internet big data.

articleTitle: Leveraging Concept-Driven Pre-Training Model for Shot-Text Conceptualization Task
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: The conceptualization of short-texts is playing an increasingly important role in text comprehension and other applications, with the aim of mapping a short-text to a set of pre-defined concepts. This work investigates and measures the adaptations of pre-training driven model in short-text conceptualization task. To this end, we discreetly design a flexible architecture as well as the corresponding procedure flow, to absorb and adopt two objectives (Concept Association Reasoner (CAR) objective and Masked-Concept Language Model (MCLM) objective respectively) into conventional pre-training architecture (e.g., BERT tested here), which have been verified on other Natural Language Processing domains. Finally, we evaluate the proposed model using several standard short-text conceptualization datasets and metrics, and experimental results showed that our model outperformed the most advanced models on real-world datasets. Especially, empirical results verify the contributions of disambiguation released by the aforementioned objectives related with concept semantics.

articleTitle: GAN-IVDS: An Intrusion Detection System for Intelligent Connected Vehicles Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace (DSC)
abstract: This paper proposes an anomaly detection algorithm based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for intrusion detection in Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs). To address the imbalance between normal network traffic and attack traffic in vehicular networks, as well as the difficulty in collecting attack data, we train the neural network solely with normal traffic.
